title: What an annotation element may declare

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: An annotation needs to carry several tag names. Which element declaration compiles?

options.says: Collections are not allowed as element types, and List.of() is not a compile-time constant either.
Wrapper types such as Integer are not allowed, and neither are arrays of them; the page says to use primitives.
String is an allowed element type, a one-dimensional array of it is too, and an empty array is a valid default.

questions.stem: An optional element of an annotation should mean "not given" by default. How is that declared?

options.text: String value() default ""; with the empty string as a sentinel.
options.says: An element cannot default to null, so a sentinel value such as "" or -1 is the page's fix.

options.text: String value() default null; with null as the default.
options.says: null is not allowed as an element default: this line is a compilation error.

options.text: Optional<String> value(); with an empty Optional.
options.says: Optional is not one of the allowed element types, so this element does not compile.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: Annotation elements may only be primitives, String, Class, enums, annotations or one-dimensional arrays of these, so a List element does not compile.
An annotation element cannot default to null, so a sentinel such as "" or -1 stands in for it.
